title: EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation becomes applicable
what_happens: PFAS limits on food-contact packaging take effect with no transition period for non-compliant stock; conformity, minimisation and EPR requirements apply to any packaging placed on the EU market. The European Commission's Aug. 1 second-edition FAQ clarified that packaging already produced or in stock before Aug. 12 does not need to be destroyed or relabeled provided it isn't newly placed on the market after that date, and that enforcement will begin with a warning/corrective-action opportunity rather than immediate penalties.
why_watch: Applies regardless of origin, so any EU-bound product or packaging component must comply from this date.
resolution: Became applicable Aug. 12, 2026 as scheduled: PFAS limits on food-contact packaging, conformity/EPR registration and minimisation requirements now apply to any packaging newly placed on the EU market. Per the European Commission's Aug. 1 FAQ, pre-Aug.-12 stock does not need to be destroyed or relabeled, and enforcement begins with a warning/corrective-action step rather than immediate penalties.

title: New York Governor's decision on the GRAS ingredient-disclosure bill
what_happens: Signature or veto due on S.1239F/A.1556G. Legal/trade-press coverage confirms the bill has not yet been formally presented to the Governor; once presented she has 10 days (excluding Sundays) to act, but under NY procedure the Legislature can hold delivery until year-end, giving a statutory backstop of Dec. 31, 2026. No presentment date has been reported yet, so the decision could come at any point between now and then. IDFA has written urging a veto.
why_watch: Would be the first state law mandating disclosure of self-affirmed GRAS safety data, and a likely template for other states.

title: Senate floor action on the Childhood Diabetes Reduction Act of 2026
what_happens: Bill advanced out of the Senate HELP Committee 12-10 and awaits a full Senate vote; would require front-of-pack warning labels on high sugar, saturated fat and sodium products.
why_watch: Thresholds would directly implicate whole milk, butter, full-fat cheese and sweetened dairy; the pre-floor-vote window is when positioning matters.

title: Senate Agriculture Committee markup of Farm Bill 2.0 (Agricultural Act of 2026)
what_happens: Committee vote failed 10-11 on Aug. 6 over an unrelated SNAP payment-error-rate dispute (dairy title was not the sticking point). The Senate returns from its late-summer recess Monday, Sept. 14; Chairman Boozman says he wants the committee to reconvene and hold the retry markup within a day or so of that return, pending the return of absent GOP Sens. McConnell (recovering from a fall, not expected back before mid-September) and Tuberville.
why_watch: Mandatory dairy-manufacturer cost/yield reporting tied to FMMO pricing, plus reauthorization of the Dairy Indemnity Payment Program and Dairy Promotion and Research Board through 2031, remain pending in the stalled bill.

title: US tariffs on Canadian imports including dairy take effect
what_happens: 50% Section 338 tariffs (signed by proclamation July 20, 2026) on Canadian-origin whey products, milk protein concentrates, lactose, casein/caseinates and milk powders were scheduled to take effect just after midnight Wednesday, Aug. 19; cheese, butter, yogurt, fluid milk/cream, sour cream and ice cream are exempted. UPDATED Aug 19 (early morning scan): Trump announced via Truth Social late Tuesday evening, Aug. 18 — under two hours before the deadline — that the tariffs are paused for three days, citing a deal with Canada "subject to the finalization of documents." PM Carney confirmed the pause, calling it "substantial progress" while cautioning important administrative/documentation work remains before the deal is finalized. The pending deal reportedly involves Canada addressing US concerns on dairy tariff-rate quotas and removing retaliatory bans on US alcohol, among other items. UPDATED Aug 19 (afternoon scan): Trump told reporters he has "come to a deal with Canada" and called it a "very fair deal for both"; Canada's Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc said he is "very confident" on the dairy piece specifically, stating "we need to protect supply management" and that "the supply management regime remains entirely intact." UPDATED Aug 19 (later afternoon scan): Multiple outlets (Bloomberg, CP24, CNN) now consistently report the pause runs to end of day Friday, Aug. 21, not Aug. 22 as earlier Axios-sourced reporting suggested; the Aug. 21 date is now treated as the working checkpoint. Quebec Premier Christine Fréchette publicly reiterated that dairy supply management is a provincial "red line," underscoring that Canada's political room to concede on dairy market access remains narrow even as both leaders describe the broader deal in positive terms. Deal is not yet finalized; if talks collapse before the checkpoint, the tariffs could still take effect.
why_watch: Whether the pending US-Canada deal is finalized by the Aug. 21 checkpoint determines whether the 50% tariff on Canadian-origin dairy ingredients takes effect at all. Canada's trade minister says supply management is untouched, but a Quebec premier's public red-line comment signals continued domestic political sensitivity on the Canadian side; IDFA and NMPF have both issued public statements urging a swift resolution.

title: New York Governor's decision on the Food Date Labeling Reform Act
what_happens: A7291B/S7618B passed both houses of the NY Legislature on June 2, 2026 and awaits presentment and the Governor's signature or veto; under NY procedure the Legislature can hold delivery until year-end, giving a statutory backstop of Dec. 31, 2026, with no presentment date yet reported. The bill would replace confusing 'sell by' dates with uniform 'Use By' (safety) and 'Best if Used By' (quality) labels on food produced after July 1, 2028; infant formula and alcoholic beverages are exempted.
why_watch: Would make New York the first state with a uniform two-tier date-labeling standard, a likely template nationally; the 2028 compliance date means packaging and labeling lead-time decisions start well before then.

title: New York Governor's decision on the infant formula/baby food heavy-metal testing and disclosure bill
what_happens: A9026/S8701 passed both houses of the NY Legislature (reported mid-2026) and would require infant formula and baby food manufacturers to test monthly for lead, arsenic, cadmium and mercury and publicly disclose results; it awaits presentment and the Governor's signature or veto. As with New York's other pending food bills, the Legislature can hold delivery until year-end, giving a statutory backstop of Dec. 31, 2026; no presentment date has been reported yet. Consumer Reports and state legislators are pushing for a signature, while the infant-formula industry is expected to lobby for a veto.
why_watch: A third pending New York food-safety/disclosure bill awaiting Hochul's signature alongside the GRAS-disclosure and date-labeling bills; would make New York the first state to mandate heavy-metal testing and disclosure for infant formula, a precedent-setting model for ingredient-safety transparency that trade groups elsewhere would watch closely.

title: FDA's mandatory GRAS-notification proposed rule — Federal Register publication
what_happens: UPDATED: Trade-press and health-policy reporting on Aug. 10 (Food Safety Magazine, STAT News) clarifies the rule (RIN 0910-AJ02) is being filed for Federal Register publication this week — Aug. 11 — not December as earlier reporting anticipated; December was a misread of the comment-period close, not the publication date. Once published it opens a 120-day public comment period (see companion watch item for the close date). HHS Secretary Kennedy publicly announced the proposal Aug. 10, shifting GRAS notification from voluntary to mandatory.
why_watch: Publication starts the comment clock on the biggest change to the GRAS pathway in decades, affecting nearly every food and dairy ingredient supplier that relies on self-affirmed GRAS determinations — four months sooner than the company's tracking assumed.
resolution: Published in the Federal Register Aug. 11, 2026 as scheduled (Document 2026-16296, Docket FDA-2025-N-3262), opening the 120-day comment period.

title: Comment period closes on FDA's mandatory GRAS-notification proposed rule
what_happens: FDA is accepting public comments on the proposed mandatory GRAS-notification rule (RIN 0910-AJ02, Docket FDA-2025-N-3262) for 120 days following its confirmed Aug. 11, 2026 Federal Register publication (Document 2026-16296). Close date calculated from the confirmed 120-day window; watch for the official Federal Register notice text to confirm the exact date.
why_watch: Last opportunity to submit formal comments before FDA can move to finalize the biggest change to the GRAS pathway in decades; ingredient-safety, regulatory and legal teams need lead time to prepare a submission.

title: FDA ultra-processed food definition — outcome of OIRA review
what_happens: FDA/HHS sent a 'Proposed Definition of Ultra-Processed Food' whitepaper to OIRA on August 3, 2026, filed as a notice (not a rule; no legal deadline). On Aug. 10, HHS and USDA publicly confirmed the definition has been submitted for final government review, but its content, and any rule, guidance, or timeline, still has not been released. HHS Secretary Kennedy has said it could become the basis for a front-of-pack red-yellow-green labeling system.
why_watch: Would be the definitional foundation for any future UPF-based labeling or program restriction, running in parallel with the Sanders and Booker/Blumenthal Senate warning-label bills.

title: Public comment period closes on California SB 54's draft EPR program plan
what_happens: Circular Action Alliance's draft statewide Extended Producer Responsibility program plan for SB 54 (California's packaging and plastic EPR law) is open for public comment through August 14, 2026; a final plan is due to CalRecycle in October 2026.
why_watch: SB 54 is the largest state EPR packaging law now in effect; the program plan sets the fee structure and compliance mechanics that determine actual cost to packaged-food manufacturers, and other EPR states are watching California's approach as a template.
resolution: Comment period closed Aug. 14, 2026 as scheduled. Circular Action Alliance will review comments as it prepares the final program plan, due to CalRecycle by October 2026 — that filing is what will actually set the fee structure and compliance mechanics producers face; projected 2027-2031 program costs run $9.3B-$17.2B, funded entirely through producer fees.

title: Douglas, AZ port reopens to Mexican cattle imports under New World screwworm safeguards
what_happens: USDA reopens the Douglas, Arizona port of entry to livestock trade from Mexico under strict New World screwworm inspection protocols — the first step in a phased reopening; Santa Teresa and Columbus, NM ports would follow if no problems arise.
why_watch: First reopening of Mexican cattle imports since the border was closed in May 2025 over screwworm; a new detection near the border could reverse the reopening and re-tighten the cattle and dairy-replacement-heifer supply chain.

title: Ruling expected in Oregon packaging-EPR constitutionality trial (NAW v. Feldon)
what_happens: Following a five-day bench trial in July and post-trial briefs filed July 31, Judge Michael H. Simon skipped oral argument and ordered narrow supplemental briefing (due Aug. 7) on whether the law's small-public-body exemption is facially discriminatory under the Dormant Commerce Clause. A ruling is expected by end of August.
why_watch: First full federal trial testing the constitutionality of a state packaging EPR law; described as a bellwether that could reshape or invalidate elements of EPR programs across all seven states that have enacted them (CA, CO, MD, ME, MN, OR, WA).

title: USDA proposed rulemaking to rewrite bioengineered food disclosure rule
what_happens: A federal court ruled USDA's exemption of highly refined bioengineered ingredients (e.g., refined corn oil, sugar) from mandatory GMO disclosure was arbitrary, and that QR-code-only compliance is unlawful; USDA's Unified Agenda reportedly targets a proposed rule as soon as August 2026, with the challenged provisions void by Jan. 1, 2028 absent a lawful replacement.
why_watch: Would broaden mandatory bioengineered-ingredient disclosure to more processed foods, including dairy products relying on refined sweeteners or oils, and bar QR-code-only labeling — a compliance approach some manufacturers use.

title: Colorado's response to NAW's preliminary-injunction motion in its packaging-EPR lawsuit
what_happens: The National Association of Wholesaler-Distributors sued Colorado (CDPHE) on July 30, 2026 challenging the constitutionality of the Producer Responsibility Program for Statewide Recycling Act (HB 22-1355) on First Amendment (compelled association/dues to Circular Action Alliance) and due-process grounds, and moved Aug. 5 for a preliminary injunction to bar enforcement and defer EPR payment obligations. Colorado's response to that motion is due Sept. 16, 2026.
why_watch: Third state EPR program NAW has challenged after Oregon and California; Oregon's court already granted NAW a partial preliminary injunction, so a similar result in Colorado would extend court-ordered relief from EPR enforcement to a second state ahead of the pending Oregon bellwether ruling (also on this watch list) and add to the litigation risk overhang on all seven EPR states.

title: FDA final rules revoking dairy standards of identity
what_happens: FDA proposed revoking 18 standards of identity for dairy products in July 2025 (RIN 0910-AJ11); the 2026 Unified Regulatory Agenda targets final rules on this and a companion revocation covering other food categories for November 2026.
why_watch: Would remove mandatory compositional/formulation requirements for multiple dairy product categories, giving manufacturers more formulation flexibility while changing the baseline other companies' product and private-label claims are measured against.

title: D.C. Circuit appeal of EPCRA farm air-emissions reporting exemption
what_happens: Environmental groups' appeal of the district court ruling upholding EPA's exemption of factory-farm ammonia/hydrogen sulfide emissions from EPCRA reporting is proceeding before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit; oral arguments expected this fall or possibly not until spring 2027, with no date set yet.
why_watch: A reversal would reinstate EPCRA air-emissions reporting obligations for larger dairy and livestock operations that the industry has spent years litigating to avoid; NMPF and dairy groups are tracking closely.
